implementation_notes: Go has no operator overloading, so the query object is a builder value: squirrel predicates (Eq, Gt, And, Or) compose into a SelectBuilder whose ToSql renders the statement and its []any arguments, which database/sql executes through driver placeholders; the builder is a plain struct, so it can be stored and passed like any other Go value. What replaces the classic object graph is structs plus method chaining, and hand-written SQL with placeholders stays justified when the statement is fixed or when the builder's rendering gets in the way.
code_sketch:
q := squirrel.Select("id", "name").From("customer").
    Where(squirrel.Eq{"status": "active"})
if minAge > 0 {
    q = q.Where(squirrel.Gt{"age": minAge})     // reassign: chaining returns copies
}
sqlStr, args, err := q.PlaceholderFormat(squirrel.Dollar).ToSql()
rows, err := db.QueryContext(ctx, sqlStr, args...)
pitfalls: Builders share backing slices, so two builders derived from one base alias each other, and dropping a returned builder loses the clause silently.
PlaceholderFormat must match the driver ($1 for PostgreSQL, ? for MySQL) or arguments bind to the wrong slots.
Table and column names cannot be parameters: keep them constant or whitelist them, never take them from user input.
